environment.tt_metal_source_revision_note: The release image does not embed a source revision; this is the repository's prior source audit revision for the pinned image.

measurement.question: Can one compute kernel select math fidelity per operation or iteration?
measurement.reference_scope: Pinned tt-metal release source audit; no board execution
measurement.source_audit_method: Read the descriptor, JIT, public compute, and Blackhole LLK sources from the pinned-release source audit.
measurement.conclusion: ComputeConfigDescriptor selects one math fidelity per compute KernelDescriptor. The public matmul_block_init and matmul_block APIs do not accept a fidelity argument and both use the compile-time MATH_FIDELITY descriptor. The Blackhole LLK wrappers expose fidelity as a C++ template parameter, so one compute-kernel source can contain matching HiFi2 and HiFi3 LLK specializations and reinitialize the matmul MOP between operations. This is compile-time specialization, not a runtime fidelity switch, and requires a custom direct-LLK path rather than the public matmul_block wrappers.

findings.evidence: ComputeConfigDescriptor has one math_fidelity field, and ComputeKernel::set_build_options copies that field into the JIT build options for the compute kernel.
findings.result: One fidelity per compute kernel descriptor.

findings.evidence: The JIT emits constexpr ckernel::MathFidelity MATH_FIDELITY into the generated compute descriptors.
findings.result: The descriptor value is compile-time state visible to the whole compute-kernel translation unit, not a runtime operation argument.

findings.evidence: matmul_block_init invokes llk_math_matmul_init<MATH_FIDELITY, MM_THROTTLE>, and matmul_block invokes llk_math_matmul<MATH_FIDELITY, MM_THROTTLE>. Neither public function has a math-fidelity parameter.
findings.result: The existing matmul_block path cannot switch fidelity per operation or iteration.

findings.evidence: llk_math_matmul_init<math_fidelity> forwards the template value to _llk_math_matmul_init_<math_fidelity>, and llk_math_matmul<math_fidelity> forwards it to _llk_math_matmul_<math_fidelity>. The LLK implementation derives fidelity phases and MOP structure from that template value.
findings.result: A custom compute source can instantiate distinct matching fidelity pairs and reinitialize the LLK matmul state at an operation boundary.

findings.evidence: The LLK documentation requires _llk_math_matmul_ to use matching template arguments after _llk_math_matmul_init_. The fidelity controls replay phases and address-mod state.
findings.result: The HiFi2/HiFi3 path must pair init and execute at the same fidelity; changing only init or only execute is not valid.

decision_for_stage_2.use_single_kernel: yes, subject to board JIT validation
decision_for_stage_2.implementation_route: Direct matching llk_math_matmul_init<F> and llk_math_matmul<F> specializations behind a small compute-kernel helper.
decision_for_stage_2.runtime_switch: not available; choose the specialization at compile time at each source-level operation boundary
decision_for_stage_2.fallback: If the pinned image rejects the direct-LLK source or the board run is not live, use two diagnostic launches and mark throughput as out of scope.

limitations: This record is source evidence only and does not establish that the custom direct-LLK source compiles or runs on p150a.
No host or board execution was used for this audit.
